name: Remote Directory Browser
description: Provides a controlled, source-neutral browser for choosing one folder from bounded remote directory snapshots without a native picker.

states: Inspect source identity, clickable breadcrumbs, bounded child folders with hidden-folder disclosure, in-place editable-path filtering, explicit cancellation, and current-folder selection.
Inspect the last canonical directory snapshot retained while navigation is loading and every navigation or selection decision is disabled.
Inspect inline bounded failure recovery with the attempted absolute path and last canonical folder list still visible.
Inspect the complete directory browser interaction and actions in Simplified Chinese.

useWhen: A trusted adapter can provide bounded read-only folder snapshots but the initiating client cannot use the source machine's native folder picker.
A remote connection flow must let a person discover and select one folder after authentication.
avoidWhen: The initiating client can and should use a native local folder picker owned by the same machine.
The workflow needs file selection, file contents, folder creation, deletion, renaming, or any other filesystem mutation.
invariants: The component is controlled presentation only and grants no filesystem, transport, authentication, or durable Project authority.
Breadcrumb and child-folder navigation emit only paths supplied by the current canonical snapshot; editable paths remain explicit user input for the adapter to validate.

Breadcrumbs and precise path entry are mutually exclusive projections of one location control: requesting edit replaces the complete source-and-breadcrumb bar with one full-width path input of identical block size, retains the last canonical folder snapshot, and moves the path-navigation action into the existing footer.

Opening precise path entry seeds the canonical directory as a continuation prefix with one trailing path separator; ordinary focus departure or Escape discards the uncommitted draft and restores breadcrumbs, while focus moving to the footer Go action or a filtered folder row preserves the intended activation.

A direct-child path fragment filters only the current bounded canonical snapshot; an ambiguous partial match requires selecting a matching folder or completing the path, while an exact candidate or unlisted absolute path remains explicitly navigable.

Dot-prefixed child folders are omitted from the default low-noise list, remain available through one explicit Show hidden folders control, and are also discoverable when precise path input begins with a dot.
The folder viewport keeps one bounded block size across ordinary, filtered, empty, and loading projections so row-count and progress changes do not resize the Dialog.

A navigation request keeps the last canonical snapshot legible, disables all navigation and selection decisions, and layers a non-resizing visual progress indicator plus localized assistive status inside the stable folder viewport instead of fading the complete task or inserting a visible status-text row.
A failed navigation retains the last canonical snapshot, attempted path, and a localized bounded reason without exposing provider diagnostics.
The browser exposes folders only and contains no file-content, filesystem-mutation, generic-command, or terminal behavior.

Folder rows use valid list semantics and every action is keyboard reachable. In breadcrumb mode, unmodified Enter chooses the current folder and the footer shows accurate Enter and Escape hints; in path-edit mode, Enter or the footer Go action submits the path, while Escape restores the canonical path draft and breadcrumb representation without cancelling the outer folder task.
